# **Global Remote Compensation Policy Framework for 2026** *Balancing Cost-of-Labor Logic, Internal Fairness, and Regulatory Transparency Across 30 Jurisdictions* --- ## **Executive Summary: A New Era of Transparent, Adaptive, and Compliant Global Pay** A fully remote software company operating across 30 countries in 2026 faces a **triple convergence**: 1. **Market Friction**: Public salary comparisons on platforms like Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, and internal Slack threads erode trust when location-adjusted pay bands are exposed. 2. **Regulatory Pressure**: New transparency laws require detailed pay information disclosure in multiple jurisdictions, including: - **EU**: Pay Transparency Directive 2023/972 (in force 2026) - **Canada**: Ontario Pay Transparency Act 2018 + federal Wage Transparency Act 2025 - **UK**: Gender Pay Gap Reporting (Extended to Ethnicity & Disability from 2026) - **Australia**: Fair Work Legislation Amendment 2024 (Protecting Worker Entitlements) - **Ireland**: Gender Pay Gap Information Act 2022 (Enforced 2025–2026) 3. **Ethical Pressure**: Rising employee activism and collective demands for “real” pay equity—not just band alignment—threaten morale and retention. ### **The Challenge: How to Set Pay in 2026?** | **Traditional Model** | **2026 Realities** | **Friction Points** | |-----------------------|--------------------|------------------------| | Location-adjusted bands | Public exposure via tech forums | “Why does Warsaw < Lisbon < Berlin?” | | Cost-focused hiring | Regulatory pay transparency | Cannot hide band differentials | | Static benchmarks (e.g., Mercer, Radford) | Real-time labor market data (LinkedIn, Levels) | Bands outdated within weeks | | Internal confidentiality | External Disclosure Requirements | Must publish band ranges and averages | > **Result**: The company is caught between **cost discipline**, **regulatory compliance**, and **employee expectations**—with no single formula that satisfies all three. --- ## **Core Principles for the Compensation Framework** We adopt **Four Guiding Principles**: | **Principle** | **Definition** | **Implementation Requirement** | |---------------|----------------|----------------------------------| | **Regulatory Primacy** | All compensation policies comply with local law first | Comply with EU 2023/972, Canada Wage Transparency Act, etc. | | **Proportional Equity** | Fairness is judged relative to peers, role, and contribution—not absolute pay | Use **Pay Fairness Score** (0–100) per employee | | **Dynamic Benchmarking** | Bands updated quarterly using real-time labor market data | Use **AI-powered compensation intelligence engine** | | **Radical Transparency** | Pay bands, individual scalar ranges, and company-wide pay analytics are disclosed internally and externally where required | Public pay transparency report annually; full band disclosure in 15 jurisdictions | --- ## **1. Compensation Architecture: A Four-Layer Model** To address internal fairness and external transparency, we redesign pay using **four interdependent layers**: > ![Compensation Architecture Diagram] > > **Layer 1: Role & Leveling** > **Layer 2: Market Benchmark with Temporal Adjustment** > **Layer 3: Local Cost-of-Living & Social Contribution Adjustments** > **Layer 4: Performance & Profit Sharing Scalar** | **Layer** | **Purpose** | **Components** | **Publishing Level** | |-----------|-------------|----------------|------------------------| | **1. Role & Leveling Framework** | Standardize roles and progression | Title, level, scope, autonomy, impact | Internal only | | **2. Market Benchmark Score (MBS)** | Align pay to global tech labor market | Base = median market (Radford/Levels/LinkedIn), adjusted for remote premium | Internal: Per employee range
Public: Aggregated by role and level | | **3. Local Market Adjuster (LMA)** | Reflect local labor market realities and cost of living | LMA = f(GDP/capita, unemployment, talent density, tax burden) | Internal only | | **4. Performance Scalar (P-Scalar)** | Recognize individual contribution and proficiency | P-Scalar: 0.8–1.2 (calibrated annually)
Profit-sharing: 5–15% company-wide | Internal only | --- ## **2. Role & Leveling Framework: The Foundation** We adopt a **global competencies-based leveling system** aligned with: - **Radford Global Roles** (SWE → Staff Engineer → Principal) - **Levels.fyi** public benchmarking - **IC → M → EM** progression paths ### **Standardized Engineering Levels (Excerpt)** | **Level** | **Title** | **Scope** | **Salary Band Floor (Base)** | **Complexity** | |-----------|-----------|-----------|-------------------------------|----------------| | IC3 | **Software Engineer** | 1–2 small features, bug fixes, documentation | $55k–85k | Low | | IC4 | **Senior Software Engineer** | Own a module, lead small team, mentor | $85k–135k | Medium | | IC5 | **Staff Software Engineer** | Own 1 massive feature or 2 critical systems | $135k–200k | High | | M2 | **Engineering Manager** | 3–5 IC reports, owns roadmap | $140k–210k | High | | EM3 | **Director of Engineering** | 2 managers, owns product line | $180k–280k | Executive | > **Key Addition**: All roles include a **"Remote Readiness Score"** (RRS) — 0–100 rating of: > - Time zone spread > - Meeting burden > - Async tooling maturity > - Language requirements > > RRS influences junior-level pay floors to compensate for coordination overhead. ### **Why Standardized Leveling?** - Enables **consistent benchmarking** across countries - Prevents "manager bias" in title inflation - Provides **career path clarity** — especially for remote employees - Helps enforce **internal equity** when comparing salaries globally > **Example**: > - A **Staff Engineer in Warsaw (IC5)** with RRS=65 gets a higher base floor than IC5 in Lisbon (RRS=40) to reflect coordination complexity. --- ## **3. Market Benchmark Score (MBS): Dynamic, Transparent, Real-Time** ### **Definition** MBS = **Median Market Compensation (Radford/Levels.ai) × Remote Premium × Equity Buffer** | **Component** | **Source** | **Frequency** | **Data Freshness** | |---------------|------------|----------------|---------------------| | Median Market Rate (MMR) | Levels.ai API + LinkedIn Salary Insights | Real-time | 7-day rolling update | | Remote Premium | Internal regression model (meeting load, async skills, time zone gap) | Quarterly | Mailed survey + tooling analytics | | Equity Buffer | Based on company performance, retention risk | Annual | Board approval | ### **MBS Formula** > **MBS = MMR × (1 + Remote Premium) × (1 + Equity Buffer)** > **Example (IC4 in 2026)**: > - MMR (Portugal): $95,000 > - Remote Premium (Lisbon → Global): +10% (due to global on-call, cross-timezone alignment) > - Equity Buffer: +5% (top-tier talent retention need) > - **MBS = $109,250** ### **Market Intelligence Engine (MIE)** We deploy an **AI-powered compensation intelligence platform** (built with): - **APIs**: Levels.ai, Radford, LinkedIn Insights, Glassdoor, Payscale - **Model**: XGBoost regressor trained on 500k global tech salaries - **Features**: Title, level, years of experience, company size, remote status, language requirements, patent/IP output, open-source contribution - **Output**: **Predicted Market Rate (µ)** with **90% Confidence Interval [µ – σ, µ + σ]** > **Use**: > - Set band floors at **MMR – 10%** (for hiring) > - Band ceilings at **MMR + 20%** (for high performers) > - Update bands **quarterly** based on inflation and attrition signals --- ## **4. Local Market Adjuster (LMA): Reflecting Local Conditions** While MBS ensures global market parity, LMA adjusts for: | **Factor** | **Weight** | **Source** | **Publishing Level** | |------------|------------|------------|------------------------| | Local Market Stress (unemployment rate, talent competition) | 30% | OECD, World Bank, Eurostat | Internal only | | Cost of Living (rent, groceries, transport relative to Warsaw) | 40% | Numbeo API, Eurostat HICP | Internal only | | Social Contributions (health insurance, pension, tax burden) | 20% | Local tax authority, Mercer | Internal only | | Legal Compliance Floor (minimum wage, sector-specific floors) | 10% | National labor law | Internal only | ### **LMA Formula** > **LMA = Σ(Weight_i × Local Adjustment_i)** > Clamped between 0.85 and 1.15 to prevent extreme distortions > **Example (Berlin)**: > - Local talent shortage: +10% > - COL: +12% (vs. Warsaw base) > - Social costs: -3% (employer tax burden similar) > - Compliance floor: 0% > - **LMA = 1.19** > **Final Role-Specific Salary Range**: > **Minimum = MBS × LMA = $109,250 × 1.19 = $129,998** > **Maximum = $109,250 × 1.19 × 1.20 = $155,996** --- ## **5. Performance Scalar (P-Scalar) and Profit Sharing** ### **P-Scalar: 0.8–1.2 (Individual Contribution)** Calculated via **calibrated self + peer + manager review** (not forced ranking): | **Dimension** | **Weight** | **Data Source** | |---------------|------------|-----------------| | Impact (feature shipped, system stability, user growth) | 40% | Jira velocity, incidents, revenue tied to work | | Initiative (beyond role, mentoring, process improvement) | 30% | Peer nominations, async contributions (e.g., Notion pages, RFCs) | | Collaboration (mentoring, cross-team alignment, documentation) | 20% | Manager + peer feedback, meeting efficiency (via meeting embeddings in calendar data) | | Growth (skill acquisition, promotion readiness) | 10% | Training logs, project ownership, promotion readiness survey | > **Process**: > - Employees complete self-review and nominate 3 peers > - Manager synthesizes with VC data and OKR alignment > - P-Scalar determined via normalized score (mean=1.0, stdev=0.08) > - **Annual recalibration** — no greater than ±0.1 jump year-over-year ### **Profit Sharing: 5–15% of Base Salary** - **Eligibility**: All employees with ≥6 months tenure as of fiscal year-end - **Allocation**: Equal per capita share of profit pool - **Payout**: Within 30 days of annual financial close - **Augmented for High Contributors**: - P-Scalar ≥1.1 → 2x base share - P-Scalar ≥1.15 → 3x base share > **Why?** > - Aligns company success with individual contribution > - Reduces reliance on stock options (dilution cost) > - Reinforces culture of shared ownership --- ## **6. Full Compensation Formula** > **Annual Base Salary (AB) = MBS × LMA × P-Scalar** > **Total Cash Compensation (TCC) = AB + Profit Share** > **Example (Senior Engineer in Warsaw, IC4)**: > - MBS (benchmarked to Berlin): €95k > - LMA (Poland: cheap COL, high unemployment): 1.02 > - P-Scalar: 1.10 (top performer) > - **AB = €95k × 1.02 × 1.10 = €106,910** > - Profit Share: €106,910 × 15% = €16,037 > - **TCC = €122,947** --- ## **7. Pay Transparency Strategy: Beyond Legal Requirements** We move from **compliance** to **trust-building transparency**. ### **Internal Transparency Levels** | **Level** | **Audience** | **Data Shared** | **Format** | |-----------|---------------|-----------------|------------| | **Level 1: Self-View** | Individual employee | Own salary band, peers with same role/level (anonymized) | In-app +/- 3 peers | | **Level 2: Role Report** | Team >5 people | Band distribution (min, p25, median, p75, max) | Confidential TGIF deck | | **Level 3: Level-Summary** | Company-wide | Median salary by level and location (aggregated) | Quarterly email + intranet | | **Level 4: Band Matrix** | All employees | Full salary bands by role, level, remote status | Vetted PDF released to maintain anonymity | | **Level 5: Transparency Audit** | External (public) | Median salary by role and level; no individual data | Annual report (complies with EU 2023/972, Canada, UK) | ### **External Transparency (Legal + Ethical)** We comply with pay transparency laws by publishing a **Public Pay Transparency Report (PPR)** annually, including: 1. **Aggregate Pay Data by Role and Level** (e.g., "Engineering IC4: $90k–$140k median") 2. **Gender Pay Gap** (by level and location) 3. **Ethnicity Pay Gap** (where permitted) 4. **Disability Pay Gap** (where data available) 5. **CEO-to-Worker Pay Ratio** 6. **Methodology**: How bands are set, data sources, update cadence 7. **Change Log**: Why bands changed from prior year > **Template**: > > *"In 2025, the median salary for a Staff Engineer (IC5) was $165,000. In 2026, with updated MBS and LMA, the updated median is $168,000—a 1.8% adjustment, below tech market inflation of 3.2%, due to improved LMA calibration in Eastern Europe."* --- ## **8. Local Law Compliance Map (Top 10 Jurisdictions)** | **Country** | **Applicable Law** | **Required Disclosure** | **Our Compliance Action** | |-------------|--------------------|-------------------------|---------------------------| | **EU (27)** | Pay Transparency Directive 2023/972 | - Gender pay gap per establishment
- Median pay by role and gender
- Explanation of gender pay differences | Publish **gender pay gap report** per country (even for single employee) using ISO gender markers | | **Germany** | Entgelttransparenzgesetz (EnTG) | Individual may request comparison of pay to peers | Offer **in-app “Pay Comparison” tool** with anonymized peers; auto-respond within 2 months | | **France** | Index de l’égalité professionnelle | Index score 90/100 | Publish index annually; if below 75, develop corrective plan | | **UK** | Gender Pay Gap Reporting (WGEA extension) | Median hourly pay gap, quartiles, proportion of men vs women in £10k pay bands | Publish report; include narrative on remote hiring impact | | **Canada** | Wage Transparency Act (ON), similar federal law | Salary bands in job postings >5 employees; disclose pay gaps | Include **salary range in all Canadian job ads** regardless of location of role | | **Switzerland** | No federal law; cantons vary | Zurich canton: disclosure in internal audits | Voluntarily publish canton-level median by role | | **Australia** | Fair Work Legislation Amendment 2024 | Publish gender and ethnicity pay gaps for employers >100 | Compile data via HRIS (BambooHR) and publish on careers page | | **Ireland** | Gender Pay Gap Information Act 2022 | Publish quartiles, gap by gender, median earnings | Full report + narrative on role-level gaps | | **USA (CA, NY)** | SB 1162 (CA) + NY Pay Transparency Law | Include pay range in job postings; disclose wage gaps per EEO-1 | Publish **CA/NY ranges in job postings** and apply to global roles posted in those states | | **Brazil** | No pay transparency law; culture favoring transparency | Informal employee demands for pay data | Proactively offer **anonymized pay dashboard** by region | --- ## **9. Addressing the "Warsaw < Lisbon < Berlin" Problem** ### **The Perception Gap** - A **Senior Engineer in Warsaw** sees: - MMR Berlin: €95k - Warsaw LMA: 0.88 (low COL) - Final: €83.6k - A **Senior Engineer in Lisbon** sees: - MMR Berlin: €95k - Lisbon LMA: 1.08 (high COL, talent shortage) - Final: €102.6k - **Public perception**: "Why is Warsaw getting paid less for the same role?" ### **Our Solution: Transparent Cost-of-Labor Audit** We publish a **Cost-of-Labor Index (CLI)** annually. | **City** | **Local Salary (Base)** | **LMA** | **Purchasing Power (PPP)** | **Net Benefit** | |----------|--------------------------|---------|-----------------------------|------------------| | Warsaw | €48k | 0.88 | 0.80 | **€42k with PIP** | | Lisbon | €56k | 1.08 | 0.95 | **€53k with PIP** | | Berlin | €72k | 1.00 | 1.00 | €72k | > **Net Benefit = Local Salary × LMA × PPP Ratio** > This shows that **Lisbon engineers enjoy higher real purchasing power** than Berlin when COL is normalized. We also provide a **Total Compensation Report (TCR)** per employee: > --- > **Your Total Compensation — 2026** > - Base: €56,000 > - Profit Share: €8,400 > - Remote Premium: €6,720 > - Taxes and Benefits: -€12,300 (Portugal) > - **Net Income After Tax: €58,820** > - **Equivalent Net in Berlin: €62,000** > - **Equivalent Net in Warsaw: €54,000** > --- > > > *"Your purchasing power is 95% of a Berlin-based peer, reflecting lower local costs and our investment in your office setup."* --- ## **10. Dealing with Dynamic Market Data: Real-Time Band Updates** ### **Problem**: Bands become stale within weeks. ### **Solution: Algorithmic Band Management (ABM)** We implement an **Automated Band Update Engine**: | **Trigger** | **Action** | **Frequency** | |-------------|------------|----------------| | MBS update (Levels.ai) > ±5% | Auto-propose band adjustment | Weekly | | Turnover in role >15% YoY | Flag low hiring competitiveness | Monthly | | Attrition rate >10% YoY for level | Raise band floor by 3% | Quarterly | | Profit-sharing payout >15% | Freeze band increases; reallocate to equity | Annually | > **Governance**: > - CPO + Compensation Lead review delta each quarter > - Employee Slack channel (#pay-questions) for feedack > - Final decision made by CPO with binding arbitration by external compensation advisor (e.g., Radford) --- ## **11. Cross-Border Compensation Equality: Avoiding "Expat-Style" Bait-and-Switch** We avoid **location-based pay bands disguising nationality bias**. ### **Rule**: All employees are paid based on **role skill level and local market**, **not citizenship**. > **Exceptions**: > - **Hardship allowances** (e.g., remote in high-risk zone) — <5% of base > - **Talent scarcity bonus** (e.g., Python/C++ experts in niche markets) — <10% > - **Tax optimization**: Platform handles all tax compliance; no off-payroll schemes > **Anti-Bias Measure**: > - **Anonymized pay audit**: Strip names, review gender/ethnicity/region gaps quarterly > - **Blind band setting**: Compensation team does not know employee nationality > - **External benchmark**: Use third-party (e.g., Mercer) to review band fairness --- ## **12. Communication Strategy: From Secrecy to Trust** ### **Internal Campaign: "Pay with Purpose"** | **Channel** | **Message** | **Timeline** | |-------------|-------------|---------------| | **Onboarding** | "You’re joining a company that pays above market in your location, with profit sharing and transparent bands." | Day 1 | | **Quarterly All-Hands** | Present band medians, PIP explanation, profit-sharing results | Q1, Q3 | | **Slack AMA** | Compensation Lead and CPO host live Q&A on pay bands | Quarterly | | **Pay Portal** | Interactive tool: "What’s your band? How does it compare?" | Live now | | **Exit Interview** | Ask: "Did pay transparency meet expectations?" | On resignation | > **Key Message**: > *"We believe transparency builds trust. We won’t hide the numbers. We will explain the logic. We will adjust when the logic fails."* --- ## **13. Legal Risks & Mitigations** | **Risk** | **Exposure** | **Mitigation** | |----------|--------------|----------------| | **Discrimination claims** (gender, race) | High (violation of Title VII, Equality Act, EU directives) | Publish pay transparency report; conduct annual equity audit | | **Retaliation for pay discussions** | Medium | Explicitly legalize and protect pay talks (NLRA, WHO) --- ## **14. KPIs: Measuring Pay Strategy Success** | **KPI** | **Target (2027)** | **Measurement** | **Owner** | |---------|--------------------|-----------------|-----------| | **Pay Fairness Score (internal survey)** | ≥85/100 | Quarterly survey (pay fairness index) | Head of People Analytics | | **Attrition Rate by Role/Level** | ≤8% YoY | HRIS data | VP People | | **Compliance Fine-Free Status** | 0 fines | Legal review | General Counsel | | **Market Salary Alignment** | ±5% of MBS within 3 months of hire | Levels.ai + internal audit | Compensation Lead | | **Public Transparency Rating** | "B+" (fairwork.org-style) | Public report card | Chief Ethics Officer | | **Profit Sharing Participation** | ≥90% eligible | Finance reports | CFO | --- ## **15. Implementation Plan (Q3 2026 – Q4 2027)** | **Phase** | **Activity** | **Timeline** | **Owner** | |-----------|---------------|---------------|-----------| | **Phase 1: Foundation (Q3 2026)** | Roll out standardized leveling framework; launch Compensation Intelligence Engine | Jul–Sep 2026 | CPO + Engineering Leadership | | **Phase 2: New Bands (Q4 2026)** | Publish Q4 2026 bands using MBS + LMA; deploy P-Scalar model | Oct–Dec 2026 | Compensation Team | | **Phase 3: Transparency Tools (Q1 2027)** | Launch internal pay portal, anonymized peer comparison, AMA schedule | Jan–Mar 2027 | People Analytics | | **Phase 4: Full Disclosure (Q2 2027)** | Release first Public Pay Transparency Report; file EU gender reports | Apr–Jun 2027 | Legal + Public Affairs | | **Phase 5: Feedback Loop (Q3–Q4 2027)** | Adjust models based on employee feedback, publish improvement report | Jul–Dec 2027 | CPO + External Advisor | --- ## **Conclusion: A Transparent, Fair, and Future-Proof Global Pay System** We have designed a **compensation framework that**: ✅ **Balances cost and fairness** using a four-layer model rooted in market data and local conditions ✅ **Turns transparency from a risk into a trust builder** through radical, well-governed openness ✅ **Reduces market friction** by explaining why gaps exist in real (not moral) terms ✅ **Meets or exceeds legal requirements** in 15+ jurisdictions ✅ **Acts like a living organism** — dynamically adjusted, ethically audited, and employee-led in feedback > **Final Message to Employees**: > *"Your pay isn’t arbitrary. It’s calculated, audited, explained—and subject to change when the market or your impact changes. We’re not perfect. But we’re committed to getting it right."* --- ## **Appendix: Sample Documents** ### **A. Internal Pay Portal Screenshot (Mockup)** ``` [Top Banner] Your Total Compensation — 2026 [Section 1] Role: Senior Software Engineer (IC4) [Section 2] Your Base: €56,000 [Section 3] Market Benchmark Score (MBS): €62,000 [Section 4] Local Market Adjuster (LMA): 0.90 [Section 5] Performance Scalar: 1.10 (Top Contributor) [Section 6] Annual Base: €60,900 [Section 7] Profit Share: €9,135 [Section 8] Peers in Same Role within 3 time zones: [Anonymized list of 7 peers with bands €58k–67k] [Section 9] Gender Pay Gap: None (50% women in role; median same) [Section 10] Calculator: "Simulate your band if you moved to Lisbon or Berlin" ``` ### **B. Public Pay Transparency Report (2026 Excerpt)** > --- > **Company Name**: Atlas Software Inc. > **Reporting Period**: Fiscal Year 2026 > **Employees**: 428 distributed across 30 countries > > **Median Total Cash Compensation (TCC) by Role**: > | Role | Median TCC | Median Market (Levels.ai) | Difference | > |------|------------|----------------------------|------------| > | Software Engineer (IC3) | $73,000 | $78,000 | -6.4% | > | Senior Engineer (IC4) | $105,000 | $112,000 | -6.2% | > | Staff Engineer (IC5) | $142,000 | $150,000 | -5.3% | > | Engineering Manager (M2) | $158,000 | $165,000 | -4.2% | > > *Note: All roles include profit-sharing. Differences reflect cost-of-living and LMA adjustments.* > > **Gender Pay Gap**: > - **Engineering**: 1.8% in favor of men > - **Non-Engineering**: 0.5% in favor of women > - *Actions*: Targeted mentorship for women in IC3–IC4 pipelines > > **Methodology**: Data sourced from HRIS (BambooHR), anonymized and aggregated. Market data via Levels.ai API, averaged over 90-day window. > > **Contact**: compensation@atlas.software > --- ### **C. Compensation Policy (Public Summary)** > **Atlas Global Compensation Principles (2026)** > 1. **Market-Aligned, Not Market-Driven**: We set pay to attract and retain top talent globally. > 2. **Transparency Over Secrecy**: We publish compensation information where required by law, and exceed it where we can build trust. > 3. **Local Market, Global Logic**: Pay reflects local conditions while maintaining internal fairness through standardized levels. > 4. **Equity, Not Equality**: We reward contribution, initiative, and impact—not just seniority. > 5. **Profit Sharing = Partnership**: Every employee shares in success. > 6. **Dynamic, Not Static**: We update bands quarterly and adjust transparently when external conditions change. > 7. **No Discrimination**: Pay decisions are blind to gender, ethnicity, nationality, or disability. --- **[END OF DRAFT RESPONSE]**
